answer.rationale: Finance demands an 18% cost cut, the assembly line has no buffer, and the contract expires in 14 days. Switching vendors (even to the proven low-cost vendor in memory_c2) introduces onboarding and integration risk at zero buffer. Adding a second source addresses resilience, not cost. Deferring the decision is not viable because the contract lapses in 14 days. Negotiating terms with the incumbent at renewal is the only path that can recover meaningful margin (as memory_c4 demonstrated) while preserving the delivery continuity that memory_c1 confirms across two prior cycles, and it can be paired with a multi-year structure to unlock volume pricing (memory_c6). Verification of memory_c2 is requested to confirm the low-cost vendor remains a credible walk-away alternative that strengthens negotiating leverage, even if the intended action is to stay and negotiate.
